assertions.rationale: The proposed CDSS includes source attribution, audit logging and version logging, and the research agenda discusses provenance. These do not specify measurement-level retention of source, units, acquisition/availability times, transformations and dataset identity. No operational provenance-preserving input adapter is reported for this composition.

Figure 4 proposes medical-image, structured-EHR and free-text inputs without specifying retention or reversible availability of native event/acquisition timestamps. Literature-search dates and Table 6 roadmap years are not observation timestamps. The unspecified temporal input contract prevents either a positive retention assertion or an assertion that timestamps are discarded.

The proposed retrieval and clinical-input workflow does not distinguish specimen/acquisition time from result-release or information-availability time, or specify availability-respecting training queries. Current guideline retrieval and clinician verification are different responsibilities. Availability semantics remain relevant to the proposed EHR-based advice, rather than being inapplicable.

The conceptual multimodal input/fusion path does not specify measured, missing or invalid indicators supplied to the model, placeholder semantics, or missing-modality processing. Out-of-scope abstention is a proposed output safeguard, not an observation-validity mask. No incompatible imputation mechanism establishing absence is reported.

Although structured EHR inputs include laboratories and vital signs, the proposed architecture does not specify carry-forward behavior, asynchronous updates, or variable-level time since true observation. Guideline currency and post-deployment monitoring do not establish measurement freshness representation.

No prediction rule in the proposed composition uses actual unequal elapsed intervals, native event timing or continuous clinical-time integration. The feedback/correction loop is a workflow proposal, and roadmap years are implementation-planning horizons. Neither establishes irregular-time prediction; no explicit uniform-spacing assumption establishes absence.

The diagram identifies observation modalities but supplies no model or rule for when, whether or why measurements occur conditional on patient or acquisition context. Retrieval grounding and clinician corrections are not a measurement-generation process. The article does not document an operational model explicitly treating sampling as ignorable either.

Figure 4's audit trail concerns versions, drift and performance surveillance. No target distinction and sampling grid, or witness-preservation test involving values, update/validity patterns, native timing and external channels, is reported. A generic audit box does not establish an observation-clock audit, and missing reporting is not evidence that a completed preprocessing audit omitted one.

Multimodal fusion and cross-site infrastructure are proposed, but source-specific clinical terminology, units and measurement definitions are not mapped to a declared target schema with traceable conversions. Feature fusion alone is not semantic/unit harmonization. No documented invalid mapping or incompatible concatenation supports an absence assertion.

For the proposed CDSS, no development cohort, train/test partition, preprocessing-fit boundary or audit of decision-time feature availability is specified. Recommendations for external validation do not establish leakage control. Literature deduplication belongs to the review methodology, not patient-level predictive-data leakage prevention. This does not contradict G01 being inapplicable to the review's own non-predictive contribution.

Sections 8.3 and Table 6 recommend federated, privacy-preserving multicentre infrastructure. The review supplies no own protocol defining participating sites, local-data retention, exchanged artifacts or federated training/query operations. The recommendation is not an implemented federation, and cited federated systems are not inherited. No explicitly central-pooling implementation establishes absence.

Figure 4 explicitly proposes modality encoders and fusion upstream of the model core. However, the paper does not define an operational observation-to-feature mapping, encoder architecture, output representation or executed path for this composition. The diagram establishes a recommended responsibility, already captured by conceptual relations, but does not meet this feature's operational evidence criteria. It is not evidence that encoders are absent.

The review discusses foundation models and future multimodal pretraining, but selects no named encoder checkpoint/version and describes no transfer or adaptation within its proposed composition. Names of surveyed models and the generic RAG-grounded model-core box do not establish foundation-encoder reuse. Training from scratch is not established either.

No context-to-target representation prediction loss is specified for the proposed CDSS. Discussion of latent diffusion, general representation learning or CLIP-style image–text pretraining does not establish a predictive-latent objective in this composition. There is no complete own training objective from which either presence or absence of a latent-target term can be established.

The proposed model has no reported predictive-representation objective, anti-collapse constraint or representation-collapse test. GAN mode collapse discussed in the literature review is a different phenomenon and supplies no evidence for this feature. Because the proposed core's training mechanism is unspecified, the parent dependency is unresolved rather than explicitly excluded; not_applicable and absent are not justified.

Reconstruction, denoising and generative imaging appear as applications of surveyed model families, not as losses of the proposed Figure 4 composition. No own loss compares reconstructed observations with observed targets. Secondary image-quality ranges do not establish such an objective, and no complete objective explicitly excluding reconstruction supports an absence assertion.

criteria_met: Figure 4 separately identifies medical images, structured EHR and free-text inputs.
The proposed workflow routes these inputs through a common modality-encoding and fusion stage.
criteria_missing: The fusion operator and modality-interaction mechanism are not specified beyond the high-level workflow.
Scope-matched execution or results establishing operational multimodal fusion are not reported.
assertions.rationale: The partial assessment is limited to the proposed architecture: identifiable modalities and an intended shared fusion stage are documented. It does not establish implemented fusion, fusion effectiveness or the capabilities of cited multimodal systems.

The proposed fusion stage does not specify availability masks, modality-quality or recency conditioning, or behavior when an input modality is missing. General multimodal recommendations do not establish availability-aware fusion, and no requirement for complete modalities is documented that would establish absence.

Figure 4 specifies information flow and clinician feedback but does not define an explicit or latent patient state, or an event history carried into a subsequent prediction/update. Retrieval storage, audit logs and a feedback arrow alone do not establish persistent evolving-state semantics.

Uncertainty/calibration guardrails and recommended uncertainty methods do not define a posterior or filtering distribution over a hidden individual state. Neither a belief-state model nor an explicitly deterministic point-state alternative is reported for this composition.

Clinician corrections are mentioned, but no prior-state propagation, observation-conditioned posterior correction, or missing-observation update rule is defined. Human review of recommendations is not evidence of a propagate–correct state estimator.

The feedback/correction loop does not specify updates to a current individual state when new measurements arrive. It could concern model corrections, retrieved content or workflow documentation; no sequential patient-state assimilation procedure or result resolves that ambiguity.

No individual parameterization, patient-specific fitting objective, measurement-driven adaptation rule or weight-update protocol is supplied. The proposed clinician feedback cannot establish patient-specific parameter adaptation, and the paper does not explicitly fix all parameters population-wide.

The review discusses multiple imaging and CDSS tasks but does not define one propagated state/checkpoint feeding at least two typed readouts. A common model-core box and broad application coverage do not establish shared-state reuse or separately trained task-specific alternatives.

No ablation or probe evaluates omitted history, variables or state representations against a prediction/decision target for the proposed composition. The nine-dimensional literature appraisal is not a state-sufficiency test, and cited systems' experiments are not transferred to this design.

EHR inputs and retrieval are proposed, but no mechanism identifies a patient's prior observation/action sequence and explains how it conditions a current inferred state or forecast. Patient-specific recommendation language does not establish longitudinal history conditioning.

No matched history-swap, history-withholding, population-prior or analogous comparison tests individual-specific predictive value for this composition. Recommendations for integrated evaluation and clinician–AI team testing do not constitute a personalization audit.

The review discusses anatomical hallucination risks, but its proposed composition specifies no memory, constraint or loss preserving anatomy, modeled entities or patient identity through transitions. Source attribution and audit logging are not identity-consistency mechanisms.

Explainability, attribution and clinician verification are discussed or recommended, but no carried state's variables or latent coordinates are mapped to inspectable clinical entities or physiology. Qualitative architecture-family explanation ratings do not establish interpretable state semantics for this composition.

No recurrent history state, temporal context window, ordered state–action memory or other mechanism retaining prior observations/actions is specified for the proposed system. The retrieval store and audit trail are not documented as temporal predictive memory; transformer terminology alone is insufficient.

Documented clinical decisions/actions and clinician accept/edit/reject choices are downstream workflow elements, not specified settable intervention inputs conditioning a future-state prediction. Free-text queries are not operationalized as intervention commands. The high-level diagram does not establish either an explicit action-conditioned predictor or a fully documented incompatible mechanism.

The review distinguishes diagnostic measurements, predictive alerts and generative recommendations, but does not supply an action vocabulary separating therapeutic, inquiry/acquisition, procedural, behavioral or operational roles with their effect channels. These output/use distinctions do not meet the typed-action criterion, and an uninterpreted action-vector implementation is not established either.

The proposed CDSS produces recommendations followed by clinician verification and a documented clinical action, but does not define an operational action schema with applicable targets, parameters, units, routes, timing, duration or reference frames. General medication-safety examples do not establish parameterized action queries for this composition.

No intervention start/stop times, administration cadence, duration or dose-schedule representation is specified for the proposed CDSS. Table 6's 0–2, 2–5 and 5+ year intervals are research-roadmap horizons, not patient intervention schedules.

The architecture does not specify joint treatment components, full-replacement versus partial-update semantics, inherited settings or preservation of linked interventions. Reviewing polypharmacy and medication interactions does not establish a coherent treatment-bundle representation in the proposed system.

Figure 4 recommends safety guardrails, out-of-scope abstention and clinician verification, but supplies no context-dependent action bounds, contraindication rules or candidate-filtering algorithm. Those general oversight requirements do not establish the action-constraint mechanism defined by this feature.

The downstream clinical decision/action box does not define encoded action variables or their mapping to specified clinical operations, device commands or executable interfaces. Clinician accept/edit/reject authority is a proposed review boundary, not a demonstrated semantic or executable action mapping.

No context-conditioned regimen coverage, overlap, propensity or mechanistic support criterion is estimated, justified and tested for this composition's recommendations. Retrieval grounding, source attribution and out-of-scope abstention are not themselves evidence of support for alternative clinical actions.

No results apply at least two specified actions to the same initial patient/history and compare predicted successors for the proposed system. The review's architecture-family comparisons and cited clinician-versus-LLM comparisons are different comparison types and cannot establish this feature or L3 capability.

The authors distinguish supervised assistance from high-stakes autonomous use and require clinician verification, but provide no action-specific assessment of physical/clinical reversibility or residual harm after execution. Rejecting a recommendation before use is not an analysis of whether a delivered intervention can be reversed.

The proposed workflow does not define a carried health-world state/history advanced to a successor under elapsed time or a declared transition coordinate. Clinician feedback and audit-monitoring arrows do not establish such a transition. Descriptions of diffusion denoising and language generation in cited model families are not temporal-dynamics evidence for this composition.

No health-world transition training objective, fitted transition parameters, learned transition structure or learned mechanistic correction is reported for the proposed CDSS. A generic LLM/predictive-model core and feedback of clinician corrections do not establish learned dynamics. The review does not supply an original trained model experiment.

No settable intervention/regime input to a health-state transition, intervention-query pathway or action-conditioned successor result is specified. The diagram's clinical decision/action is downstream of clinician review, not an evidenced conditioning input to predictive world dynamics.

No conditional random next-state process or transition sampling procedure is defined for this composition. General discussion of probabilistic generation and a proposed uncertainty/calibration guardrail do not establish stochastic world-state transitions, uncertainty decomposition or calibration.

The proposed architecture supplies no physiological equations, conservation rules, anatomical constraints, monotonicity conditions or symbolic structure constraining a transition or learned representation. Retrieving clinical guidelines is a proposed information-grounding mechanism, not a demonstrated mechanistic inductive constraint.

No mechanistic and learned dynamics components are operationally coupled with identified fixed, fitted and learned quantities. Combining encoders, retrieval, an LLM/predictive core and human review is not sufficient to establish mechanistic–learned hybrid dynamics.

The review compares architecture families and labels a generic LLM/predictive-model core, but documents no two interchangeable dynamics implementations sharing state, action, time and output semantics, and no integration or replacement test. A comparative literature table does not establish backend pluggability.

Images, structured EHR and text are proposed as multimodal inputs, but no distinct physical, spatial or temporal dynamical levels exchange states or constraints through explicit cross-scale mappings. Multimodal fusion and coverage of multiple clinical specialties do not establish coupled multiscale dynamics.

assertions.applicability_reason: The review performs literature synthesis and proposes a CDSS workflow; it does not train a dynamics model. There is no original transition-training procedure to assess for losses traversing multiple predicted transitions.
assertions.rationale: Background descriptions of generative-model training do not establish an objective implemented by this review. Clinician feedback in Figure 4 is not a specified multistep dynamics optimization.

assertions.applicability_reason: The proposed composition describes information processing and clinician verification, not primitive and higher-level health-world transitions over a declared temporal coordinate.
assertions.rationale: Architecture-family hierarchies and Table 6's 0–2, 2–5 and 5+ year research-roadmap periods are not coordinated temporal abstractions within a dynamics model.

Figure 4 names a RAG-grounded LLM or predictive-model core, but does not specify an internal-state-to-observation emission mapping for that composition. Descriptions of U-Net decoders, GAN synthesis and diffusion elsewhere concern surveyed model families and cannot establish this feature for the proposed system.

The article discusses risk scores, diagnoses, recommendations and imaging measurements, but does not define state/trajectory readout heads with named targets, units and horizons for its proposed composition. Generic predictive-model and documented-decision boxes do not establish typed outcome heads.

assertions.applicability_reason: The paper's own study is a narrative review, not an experiment evaluating a health-world successor-state predictor. Its conceptual CDSS is not subjected to prediction experiments.
assertions.rationale: Table 3's secondary classification, segmentation and generation ranges are not original future-state prediction results. No cited system's evaluation is transferred to the review.

assertions.applicability_reason: The proposed Figure 4 workflow is not a temporal simulation service and does not define successive health-world transitions or future-trajectory queries.
assertions.rationale: Its processing stages and feedback path are not generated-state recursion. Diffusion denoising steps and multistep language reasoning discussed as background are not free-running clinical rollouts.

assertions.applicability_reason: There is no original sequential prediction evaluation in which intermediate reference states could be supplied or withheld.
assertions.rationale: The review's literature-appraisal procedure and proposed clinician verification are not teacher-forced model evaluation protocols.

The proposed feedback loop routes clinician corrections back toward the model, but does not specify whether these modify retrieval content, parameters, records or a maintained state. No mechanism describes new measured evidence correcting a predicted state before a subsequent forecast. Resolving this requires an explicit state-update and forecast protocol; the feedback arrow alone is insufficient.

assertions.applicability_reason: The conceptual composition has no evaluated temporal forecast whose furthest tested extent could be recorded.
assertions.rationale: Table 6's year ranges are proposed research and implementation milestones, not evaluated prediction horizons. Search dates and diffusion sampling iterations also do not supply a clinical forecast horizon.

assertions.applicability_reason: No original free-running forecast sequence is evaluated at multiple depths, so a compounding-rollout-error test has no prediction experiment to operate on.
assertions.rationale: Proposed post-deployment drift surveillance concerns changing model or data performance over operational time; it is not an error-versus-rollout-depth experiment.

assertions.applicability_reason: The paper proposes no temporal forecast/planning service or usable rollout-length claim for its own composition. An effective forecast horizon is therefore outside this specified contribution.
assertions.rationale: Task-specific validation recommendations and roadmap year ranges are not model-specific error/calibration curves with acceptance tolerances, action support and uncertainty.

assertions.applicability_reason: The proposed system does not define future patient/world trajectories as its output or specify a temporal forecasting query.
assertions.rationale: Diverse synthetic images, stochastic language generation and a generic uncertainty/calibration guardrail do not establish coherent conditional future-trajectory samples or a joint temporal forecast distribution.

assertions.applicability_reason: No user-requested temporal forecast extent or supported rollout horizon is part of the proposed workflow, so horizon-request enforcement is not a defined responsibility in this scope.
assertions.rationale: The proposed out-of-scope abstention safeguard is generic. It is not evidence of rejecting, transparently truncating or escalating unsupported forecast-horizon requests.

Figure 4 links a generic LLM/predictive core to clinician review and a documented decision, but does not specify simulated future states or outcomes feeding ranking, search or policy learning. Clinical advice and risk-score interpretation alone do not establish future-grounded model-based decision coupling.

The composition does not report an optimizer, a learned policy using modeled consequences, an objective/search procedure or decision-control results. Retrieval grounding and clinician accept/edit/reject choices cannot substitute for those mechanisms. This is missing planning evidence, not an explicit negative claim that every possible implementation excludes a planner.

No protocol specifies computing an action plan, executing a prefix, receiving new observations and recomputing the plan with declared planning/execution horizons. The unspecified clinician-correction loop does not establish replanning. Because the parent optimizer/policy mechanism is itself unreported, its missing evidence is not converted into either explicit absence or dependency-based inapplicability.

capability_assessments.rationale: Full supplied text describes narrative synthesis and a conceptual CDSS workflow, not an implemented persistent state advanced over a health-world coordinate by learned/hybrid dynamics. There is no original WM-inspired representation experiment supporting L0, future-state evaluation supporting L1, specified-action prediction supporting L2, matched action comparison supporting L3, or WM-coupled control result supporting L4. Diffusion denoising, text generation and clinician-feedback arrows do not establish those capabilities. Decisive evidence: evidence:096:002, 009, 010 and 017.

scope.evidence_scope: Proposed Figure 4 composition only; no implementation or tested environment
scope.interpretation: Concept-stage design, not an automatic readiness label for the review and not clinical validation

gate_assessments.rationale: For this conceptual/background contribution there is no original empirical predictive system, patient-data adapter or train/test leakage claim to certify. Literature-search transparency and missing supplementary appraisal remain review-quality issues, not a passed predictive-data gate.
The review does not claim its own temporal world model. Its synthesis and CDSS diagram do not supply an operative state-transition predictor.
No multi-time world-state forecast or rollout is specified for this composition. Table 6's year ranges are research-roadmap horizons, not model horizons.

The proposed guardrail includes uncertainty/calibration, but no estimator, calibration set, target coverage, clinical tolerance, action regime or observed result establishes uncertainty acceptance. This blocks a design-assurance pass, not evidence that a tested method failed.
A downstream documented clinical action is not a settable input to a learned health-world transition. No action-conditioned or matched-alternative prediction service is reported.
No original intervention-effect estimand or causal model is proposed or evaluated. Secondary clinical-benefit accounts are not promoted into identified effects for this review.
No model-coupled optimizer or learned decision policy is specified and evaluated. Generic recommendations and clinician accept/edit/reject choices do not establish an M8 planner.

Attribution, abstention and clinician verification are proposed, but operational triggers, hazard-specific thresholds, fallback performance and evaluated fail behavior are not reported. No safety guarantee or failed safety test is inferred.
Cross-site validation and fairness audits are recommendations, not composition-level external, subgroup or shift evaluations.

Human oversight is central to the proposed design, but this composition has no actual participant study, clinician–AI team experiment or physical-environment evaluation. Cited human studies are not inherited.

Prospective patient/workflow utility is an explicit research objective, not a reported evaluation of the proposed system. No shadow, feasibility or comparative-effectiveness evidence establishes a pass.
No operational product/version is released by this review. Naming regulations and proposing audit/monitoring functions do not create a deployment, authorization or lifecycle-compliance assessment.

limitations: This is automated API model review and a skeptical second-pass consistency assessment, not independent human verification or replication.

All 21 supplied text pages were read. Visual coverage is represented by the supplied page/image review notes for all 21 pages; separately accessible page images were not available to this synthesis for a fresh inspection.

The supplied page-review notes contain chunk-local statements that other pages were unavailable. Across this submission the complete main-text page set 1–21 is supplied; those chunk-local statements are not treated as current whole-document omissions.
Supplementary Data Sheet 1, also called Supplementary Table S1, and Supplementary Data 2/S2 were advertised but not supplied or retrieved.
No external publisher, bibliographic database, repository or cited primary study was accessed.
The review contains inconsistent evidence-base counts, date windows, eligibility descriptions, RAG conclusions, bibliographic attributions and technical wording; these are preserved and queued.

The original review is unregistered, non-systematic and nonexhaustive, and acknowledges possible publication bias, overrepresentation of reviews, English-language restriction, lack of formal risk-of-bias assessment and rapid evidence obsolescence.
The descriptive nine-dimension rubric lacks sufficiently reported scoring anchors, weighting, reviewer agreement and reproducibility evidence in the supplied main article.
No original trained model, persistent health-world state, learned transition, future-state experiment, action-conditioned rollout or model-coupled control evaluation is reported.

The proposed Figure 4 architecture is not an implemented ModuleImplementation and does not demonstrate calibrated uncertainty, effective abstention, causal validity, clinical safety or prospective utility.
No original held-out actual human/clinical evaluation establishes R2. Cited retrospective, human, prospective, trial and authorization evidence is not transferred to this review.
No original model-scoped MetricResult can be populated without inventing model/cohort/split details. Secondary ranges and cited clinical quantities are retained in AnalysisFinding entities instead.

Family-level qualitative readiness and reliability ratings are not numerical comparisons, clinical thresholds, authorization determinations or proof of an unavoidable capability–reliability trade-off.
Diffusion sampling steps, language-generation operations, feedback arrows and research-roadmap year ranges are not clinical world-transition or validated rollout horizons.
Article CC BY licensing does not establish released code, open model weights, prompts or model-asset licensing.
